public_payload.normalized_proposition: If OpenAI or Anthropic die, 40% to 73% of all AI revenue and compute demand will evaporate.
conditions: if OpenAI or Anthropic or both die

statement.excerpt: OpenAI and Anthropic are both separately load-bearing companies. If either or both of them die, 40% to 73% of all AI revenue and compute demand evaporates.

from_speaker: OpenAI and Anthropic are both separately load-bearing companies
If either or both of them die
all AI revenue and compute demand evaporates
our_interpretation: Die means economic failure as an operating business able to sustain its compute purchases. The context permits a shell entity or continued access to its models, so legal dissolution is not required.
An acquisition, product retirement, or reported accounting loss alone does not establish that antecedent.
The ordinary reading requires a 40%–73% decline in both industry AI revenue and compute demand after the failure.
All AI means industry-wide activity, not only the labs' own sales or selected hyperscaler contracts.
Demand that transfers to competitors has not evaporated. Revenue must be measured consistently without changing the treatment of transactions between suppliers and customers.
The source gives no exact mapping from one-lab versus two-lab failure to the percentage endpoints, and no dated measurement window.
criteria.support_condition: After documented economic failure of either or both labs, comparable industry-wide measurements show an attributable 40%–73% loss of both AI revenue and compute demand after accounting for customer migration.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After the antecedent occurs, sufficiently complete and comparable measurements show that the predicted decline in revenue or compute demand falls outside the stated range. Different results for the two measures would require separate treatment.

evidence.locator: Prospectus summary, financial model discussion before Our Self-Reinforcing Loops
evidence.publisher: Anthropic, PBC / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
evidence.explanation: Anthropic describes continuing access to financing and compute in its filing. This weighs against assuming the failure antecedent, but does not independently establish long-term solvency.
Oracle describes an active commercial relationship with OpenAI. This does not establish economic failure, and collaboration alone cannot prove financial viability.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Documented economic failure of either lab, followed by consistent industry-wide revenue and compute-demand measurements that account for customer migration and establish the attributable change.
